videos.script: The office has one Mac. The person who used it has left, and on Monday it goes to the new designer. Ana's task is to make sure it arrives clean, and that it belongs to the office rather than to anybody. {{handover}} There is no USB stick to make this time, or not usually. Every Mac carries its own installer, in a part of the disk called Recovery, and a Mac can reinstall itself from the internet with nothing plugged in. {{recovery}} What there is instead is a lock. A Mac that was signed into somebody's Apple Account with Find My turned on stays tied to that account, even after its disk is erased. Erase it the wrong way and the new designer is stuck on the second screen, asking for a password nobody in the office knows. {{lock}} You will tell an Apple silicon Mac from an Intel one, and reach Recovery on each. You will see how APFS lays out the disk, and choose between the three ways to reset a Mac. Then you will get through Setup Assistant with the right answers, and do the handful of things every new Mac needs before somebody uses it. {{steps}} Nothing in this lesson was run on a Mac. The screens are described, and the commands are the ones you would type there. {{honest}}
